# Effort management

Binary-owned effort records and optional resources.

The awf binary owns lightweight repository-local effort records and their optional resident resources. These records coordinate local work without replacing tracked project authority.

## Claims

### `invariant: effort-record-authority`

The awf binary accepts a caller-supplied canonical slug through 32 bytes when minting a new immutable slug/UUID identity, retains canonical resident reads and command selection through 63 bytes, and durably owns otherwise-unchanged schema-2 `state.json`, always-owned `memory.md`, optional mutable protocol-v2 `activity.json`, and one optional owned real `scratch/` directory under `.awf/efforts/<slug>/`. Scratch descendants are opaque: awf never traverses, validates, lists, interprets, scaffolds, or manages them. Directory presence remains the active-effort fact; listing and selection ignore unpublished finishing reservations and `.awf/effort-archive` descendants while preserving foreign residents, and show/list/finish keep protocol-file validation strict without gating on activity or mutable checkpoint metadata. After managed topology is proven absent and the exact safely owned archive root and fully rendered self-ignore marker are validated, finish reserves the resident as `.finishing-<uuid>-<slug>` and atomically moves the complete unchanged directory without replacement to `.awf/effort-archive/<uuid>-<slug>`. The archive move releases the slug; collisions and cross-device moves refuse without copy/delete, pre-move interruption remains retryable by slug, and post-move durability uncertainty reports the exact source and destination for inspection rather than blind retry. Archived activity and scratch remain unchanged local bytes. The archive is ignored, unmanaged, non-authoritative, invisible to effort inventory, and manually disposable; awf provides no archive inventory, restore, prune, analysis, retention, force-delete, or bypass surface. The binary alone performs bounded complete-document memory reads, body-only exact edit batches, structured metadata updates, atomic memory publication, and owner-checked advisory activity mutation for active residents. Activity remains a fallible session claim and owner comparison remains advisory process consistency, never topology, authorization, a lock, lifecycle/worktree state, tracked-project authority, or protection against takeover after comparison.
Backing: test

### `invariant: managed-worktree-lifecycle`

Managed effort worktrees are stateless native-Git utilities at `.awf/worktrees/<slug>/` on `awf/<slug>`. Standalone Add leaves the complete effort unchanged on failure; default effort creation orchestrates this same Add machinery after resident publication, and the shared result carries structured path and branch facts. Integration revalidates clean target, registration, repository identity, branch, operation state, and ancestry immediately before mutation; it reports already-contained history, fast-forwards, or starts a divergent `--no-commit` merge, never tests, reviews, commits, pushes, resolves, removes, records disposition, or finishes. Remove independently inspects path, registration, and branch on every retry, requires cleanliness and target ancestry, and uses no awf force-discard path; intentional discard stays explicit native Git.
Backing: test

### `invariant: default-worktree-creation`

`awf effort new --slug <slug> <outcome-title>` without `--no-worktree` feeds the required explicit slug through resident publication, then creates the managed worktree through the same standalone Add machinery at `.awf/worktrees/<slug>/` on `awf/<slug>`, based on the invoking checkout's `HEAD` unless `--base <ref>` selects another base; `--base` is invalid with `--no-worktree`. If Add fails, orchestration classifies actual topology and invokes a narrow immutable-identity-bound deletion rollback only when path, registration, and branch are proven absent. The rollback revalidates the exact just-created UUID and slug, reserves and removes only that resident, reports typed publication outcomes, never routes through public finish, and never archives an unsuccessful creation; present or ambiguous topology, identity change, or interrupted deletion retains bytes with concrete recovery actions. Success reports the worktree path and branch and directs continuation there; `--no-worktree` reports explicit absence and keeps execution in the invoking checkout.
Backing: test

### `invariant: memory-skeleton-purpose-partition`

The binary-scaffolded memory begins with closed YAML frontmatter containing exactly `effort`, `phase`, `next`, and `updated`, using immutable slug identity, bounded nonblank single-line mutable values, and a real UTC creation/update time. Its Markdown body retains `## Brief`, append-only ordinal `## Decision log`, append-only `## Observations`, and `## Handoff log`, with each placeholder naming its contract and consumer. Bounded reads paginate the complete canonical document by one-indexed lines, cap selection at 2,000 complete lines and 50 KiB without integer overflow, stop before an omitted line, and report deterministic range, continuation, truncation, or individually unpageable-line facts. Body edit evaluates 1 through 128 individually one-MiB-bounded exact replacements against the original body, requires each old text exactly once, refuses nested or overlapping regions as one unchanged batch, applies disjoint replacements in original-position order without fuzzy fallback, and returns a deterministic diff bounded to 50 KiB. Edit preserves immutable and mutable metadata, advances `updated` once from the injected UTC clock even for a body no-op, rejects an encoded result over one MiB, and publishes body plus timestamp as one synced-sibling atomic replacement. Structured update rewrites only selected mutable metadata plus time, repairs invalid mutable values only when every invalid field is supplied and identity/boundary are safe. Publication failures distinguish the unchanged pre-replacement stages from post-replacement durability uncertainty and direct callers to read before another mutation; section headings remain unparsed by production code. Owner-scoped preview is presentation-only, fails before execution, never clocks or publishes, and cannot change normal validation. It emits one Pi-compatible four-context-line display diff using canonical source offsets; changed content is elided in complete rows, deterministic representative changed rows survive bounding, and whole changed rows or ranges use Pi's exact omission row. `truncated:true` reports only bounding loss from content elision or dropped rows and ranges; ordinary hunk separation and discarded context outside the defined four-line window never set it. Update preview omits `updated`; normal update returns the authoritative full-document diff including its actual timestamp.
Backing: test

### `rule: managed-effort-format-support`

Schema-2 effort residents, canonical YAML memory, activity protocol 2, managed worktree topology, and byte-preserving archive moves remain current lifecycle formats.
